title: Crimes Legislation Amendment (Age of Criminal Responsibility) Bill 2019
short_title: Crimes Legislation Amendment (Age of Criminal Responsibility) Bill 2019

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would raise the minimum age of criminal responsibility for Commonwealth offences from 10 to 14 years by amending federal crimes and criminal code legislation.
Children younger than 14 could not be held criminally responsible, and related forensic procedure provisions would be adjusted to reflect the new minimum age.
It would begin the day after royal assent and apply only to offences committed from commencement, while older children could still face criminal proceedings.
changes: Redundant criminal responsibility provisions in the Crimes Act and Criminal Code would be repealed.
For suspect forensic procedures, the statutory child category would cover people aged 14 to under 18.
Forensic procedures requested by foreign countries would not apply to children under 14.
summary.affected: Children involved in Commonwealth criminal matters are affected.

speeches.speaker: Zali Steggall
speeches.brief: The speech supported raising the minimum age of criminal responsibility to 14, noting that 600 children under 14 are imprisoned each year, 70% of whom are Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander, and that the international median age is 14.
